{{Short description|Polish theoretical physicist}}
'''Tomasz Robert Taylor''' (born February 23, 1954) is a Polish-American [[theoretical physicist]] and faculty at [[Northeastern University|Northeastern University in Boston, Massachusetts, United States of America]]. He obtained his PhD degree from the [[University of Warsaw|University of Warsaw, Poland]] in 1981 under the supervision of Stefan Pokorski. He is a descendant of John Taylor who originated from [[Fraserburgh]] in [[Kingdom of Scotland|Scotland]] and emigrated to the [[Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth|Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth]] c.1676.

He is known for his discovery, with [[Stephen Parke]], of [[MHV amplitudes|Parke–Taylor amplitudes]], also known as maximally helicity violating [[MHV amplitudes|(MHV) amplitudes]];<nowiki/><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Parke|first1=Stephen J.|last2=Taylor|first2=T. R.|date=1986|title=Amplitude for n-Gluon Scattering|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=56|issue=23|pages=2459–2460|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.2459|pmid=10032998|bibcode=1986PhRvL..56.2459P}}</ref> his pioneering use of [[supersymmetry]] for computing [[scattering]] [[Quantum amplitude|amplitudes]] in [[quantum chromodynamics]];<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Parke|first1=Stephen J.|last2=Taylor|first2=T. R.|date=1985|title=Perturbative QCD utilizing extended supersymmetry|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=157|issue=1|pages=81–84|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(85)91216-X|bibcode=1985PhLB..157...81P}}</ref> his seminal work, with Ignatios Antoniadis, Edi Gava and Kumar Narain, on [[Topological string theory|topological string]] amplitudes;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Antoniadis|first1=I.|last2=Gava|first2=E.|last3=Narain|first3=K. S.|last4=Taylor|first4=T. R.|date=1994|title=Topological amplitudes in string theory|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=413|issue=1|pages=162–184|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(94)90617-3|arxiv=hep-th/9307158|bibcode=1994NuPhB.413..162A|s2cid=15426291 }}</ref> his formulation, with Ignatios Antoniadis and Hervé Partouche, of the first four-dimensional [[quantum field theory]] with partial [[supersymmetry breaking]];<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Antoniadis|first1=I.|last2=Partouche|first2=H.|last3=Taylor|first3=T. R.|date=1996|title=Spontaneous breaking of N = 2 global supersymmetry|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=372|issue=1|pages=83–87|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(96)00028-7|arxiv=hep-th/9512006|bibcode=1996PhLB..372...83A|s2cid=118882758 }}</ref> his extensive studies, with Stephan Stieberger, of [[Superstring theory|superstring]] [[scattering]] amplitudes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Stieberger|first1=Stephan|last2=Taylor|first2=Tomasz R.|date=2014|title=Closed string amplitudes as single-valued open string amplitudes|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=881|issue=Supplement C|pages=269–287|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2014.02.005|arxiv=1401.1218|bibcode=2014NuPhB.881..269S|s2cid=119174893 }} and references therein.</ref>
